articleTitle: Resonant scattering of the SH-wave by the interface impedance defect in an elastic layer
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The interaction of the elastic SH-wave with the defect on the boundary joint of an elastic layer with half-space is investigated. The defect is modelled by the impedance tape on the boundary of a joint. The solution of the diffraction problem is obtained as the infinite system of linear algebraic equations by using the Wiener-Hopf technique. The corresponding characteristic equation is derived for determining the spectrum. The dependence of eigenfrequencies on the problem parameters is also presented.

articleTitle: Simultaneous quasi-RHCP and LHCP radiation in the near field of planar RFID antennas
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The concept of quasi-circular polarization (CP) of the EM field produced in the near field by a planar RFID antenna is discussed. Optimized CP near field performance is obtained by shaping the layout of periodic EM coupled strips forming the antenna aperture. It is shown that the specifically designed planar antenna can simultaneously produce the right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) and left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) in the spatially different areas of the near field zone. The results of EM simulation illustrate the mechanism of producing the quasi-CP radiation in the antenna near field zone at different distances from the antenna surface.

articleTitle: Calibration of microwave waveguide sensor for biomedical applications
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: In the present work, we propose calibration procedure for microwave waveguide-based sensor for dielectric measurements in biomedical applications. We have applied full-wave 2D modelling for calculating mappings of complex reflection coefficient from sensor to complex permittivity of a sample under test. We used water and ethanol/water mixtures with mole fractions of 0.04 and 0.08 as reference liquids both for simulation and measurements. Quality assessment function based on the least-squares fitting technique is employed in choosing of calibration from a set of modifications calculated for different sensor geometries. Our results show that required accuracy of calibration, which should be at least 2.5%, can be achieved by means of the proposed procedure. The suggested approach is intended to calibrate sensors of arbitrary geometries.

articleTitle: Energy transformation of transient field of Herzian dipole
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: On the basis of the known vector potential method in time domain the problem of transient radiation of small source of electrical current is solved. The classical solution for Herzian dipole radiation is compared with the improved one obtained previously and with precise solution calculated numerically for all distanced including the near zone of the radiator. It is proposed a new criterion of zones of transient radiation on the base of H. F. Harmuth's idea of time dependent zones.

articleTitle: Influence of the dielectric loss in a dielectric filled rotating spherical resonator on the precision of the rotation rate measurement
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The influence of the dielectric loss in the dielectric inside the resonator on the precision of the rotation rate measurement by the new resonant method is studied. The method allows using the electromagnetic field of the microwave band, that allows increasing the precision of the measurements and decreasing the geometrical dimension of the resonators. For that purpose, the boundary value problem of excitation of a rotating resonator is formulated and solved rigorously using the covariant expressions for electromagnetic fields. The frequency characteristics for the case of excitation of the resonator with electric dipole are calculated and analysed for various parameters of the dielectric filling.

articleTitle: On the theory of transition radiation of a charged particle in a waveguide with a modulated anisotropic magnetodielectric filling
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The transition radiation of a charged particle in a regular waveguide with periodically modulated anisotropic magnetodielectric medium during its passage perpendicular to the axis of the waveguide is considered. In a first approximation with respect to the small index of modulation the analytical expressions for the transverse-electric (TE) field and for the energy of transition radiation in the region of “weak” interaction between the field of radiation and the modulated filling are found. In particular, the case of a rectangular waveguide is considered. The analysis of obtained results shows, that the field in the waveguide represents the set of space harmonics with different amplitudes and in the expression for the energy loss of the particle appears member proportional to the small modulation index in the first degree.

articleTitle: Widely linear quaternion adaptive filtering in the frequency domain
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Adaptive filtering can be expanded to new numerical systems and unseen sides of physical problems can be highlighted thanks to the mathematical properties of such hypercomplex algebras. Each algebra has its own rules and operation results may not be compatible from one algebra to another. However, such peculiarities diversify algebras in a way that each of them fits specific geometrical/physical problems. In this work we propose a quaternion widely linear adaptive algorithm operating in the frequency domain. The aim is to overcome the problem of high computational cost occurring when time-domain algorithms are used. An analysis of the cost is also supplied. Finally, simulations support our proposal.

articleTitle: Complex source point beam excitation of a lossless dielectric slab
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The excitation of the guided modes of a lossless slab by a complex source point (CSP) beam is semi-analytically investigated. The goal is to compute the guided-mode powers and efficiencies as a function of problem's parameters, namely the electrical thickness, the angle of incidence, the beam aperture, and the aperture location.

articleTitle: A novel algorithm for estimation of moving target parameters with single-antenna SAR
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The idea for automatic extraction of the moving target parameters using single-antenna synthetic aperture radar is proposed. The displacements of the target are estimated from the sequence of the single-look SAR images using the Lucas-Kanade optical flow technique. It is shown that both moving target location in the SAR look and its shift direction can be extracted. In addition, the linear road segments are automatically detected from the multi-look SAR image using the Canny edge map and local pixels intensity gradient analysis. Proposed ideas are incorporated into the novel algorithm capable to unambiguously extract the moving target parameters using the single-antenna SAR system. Experimental examples obtained with X-band airborne SAR system are illustrated as well.

articleTitle: Inverse scattering with non-over-determined data
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: It is proved that the scattering amplitude A(β,α<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>), known for all β ∈ S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, where S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is the unit sphere in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, and fixed α<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> ∈ S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> > 0, determines uniquely the surface S of the obstacle D and the boundary condition on S. The boundary condition on S is assumed to be the Dirichlet, or Neumann, or the impedance one. The uniqueness theorems for the solution of multidimensional inverse scattering problems with non-over-determined data was not known for many decades. Such theorems are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Grating resonances in the scattering of light by periodically structured dielectric nanowires
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: We present the results of numerical simulation of the scattering of the H-polarized electromagnetic wave by a finite grating made of dielectric nanowires, in the visible range of light. Numerical solution uses the field expansions in local coordinates of each wire and addition theorems for cylindrical functions and has a guaranteed convergence. Numerical results are presented for the analysis of the far-field and near-field characteristics of the studied scatterers. This work is focused on the detection of the grating-type resonances in the far-field characteristics and specific near-field patterns in these resonances.

articleTitle: Polarimetric method to discriminate the drops on sizes within the resolution volume
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: In this paper we consider possibilities of radar polarimetry to solve different meteorological tasks including identification of atmospheric pfenomena microstructure and hydrometeor orientation, hydrometeors size measurement, wind related phenomena estimation. The potentials and restrictions of radar polarimetry are discussed. The approach that allows to increase informativity of polarization measuremens by distinguishing hydrometeors with similar polarization properties inside the reflecting volume and estimating their differential impact onto polarization properties of reflected signal is presented. The overvew of the polarimetric system with multiple receiving antenna system for aproach realization is done. The results are important for different practical applications of radar meteorology including drop size distribution estimate, rainfall intensity estimate, wind speed measurement, turbulence and strong wind shear detection.

articleTitle: Directional characteristics of an antenna array of monopoles on a perfectly conducting sphere
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The small-sized radiators (receivers) of electromagnetic waves on the base of the system of six equidistant radial monopoles in the equatorial plane of the conducting sphere are considered. It is shown that for the antenna the various directional patterns by switching phases of voltage sources only for two monopoles can be realized. The considered radiators can be used as a small-sized sensors and antennas for different purposes.

articleTitle: Focusing ability of a microsize graphene-based cylindrical reflector in the THz range illuminated by electromagnetic plane wave
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The scattering of the H-polarized plane wave by a two-dimensional (2-D) parabolic reflector made of graphene placed in the free space is simulated by using the Method of Analytical Regularization (MAR) technique. The total scattering cross-section and absorption cross-section are computed, together with the field magnitude in the geometrical focus of reflector. The surface plasmon resonances are observed. Besides, the focusing ability of the reflector is studied in dependence of the chemical potential of the graphene.

articleTitle: Circular waveguide with anisotropic impedance surface as an equivalent model for dielectric waveguides used in gyro-devices
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The eigenvalue problems for step-index and dielectric-lined waveguides with anisotropic cladding are transformed to the similar form as for impedance waveguide. Both problems are then reduced to separate ones, each describing either HE or EH hybrid waves. The frequencies and the fields of the hybrid waves are also determined. It is proven that HE (EH) waves behave generally like TE (TM) waves inside the core regions of both step-index and dielectric-lined waveguides regardless of the wave frequency and the waveguide parameters.

articleTitle: Design of fractal loop antenna with integrated ground plane for RF energy harvesting
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel impedance matching method for loop antenna by integrating the in-loop ground plane (ILGP). Compact Koch fractal loop is designed for ambient radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting applications at GSM1800 band. Comparing to the conventional matching method for loop antenna, the proposed ILGP doesn't require any additional layout and can easily match the impedance to 50 Ohms. The in-loop ground plane makes antenna more compact and provides high total efficiency. The performance of the proposed antenna has been verified by simulation and measurements. It should be noted that the ILGP matching method is useful for various planar loop antennas utilized for different wireless communication applications.

articleTitle: On single-mode analysis of dielectric-loaded gyrotron cavity
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Wave equations are derived for quasi-TE and quasi-TM waves of the gyrotron cavity with dielectric-coated conducting walls. The equations are valid on condition that both the wall radius and the coating thickness vary slowly along the cavity axis. Numerical calculations are performed for quasi-TE modes of the gyrotron cavity with distributed dielectric coating, which provides lower diffractive losses for high-frequency modes.

articleTitle: Formation of circularly polarized wave by impedance wire dipole located over square screen
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: For a radiating system consisting of a resonant half-wave impedance oblique wire dipole and a rectangular perfectly conducting screen the conditions guaranteeing formation of a circularly polarized wave with extremely achievable field amplitude in the set directions of the main observation planes are investigated. Computation of the far field components is based on the asymptotic solution of 3D vector problem of diffraction of the field of electric dipole on the ideally conducting rectangular screen, obtained by the method of uniform geometric diffraction theory. To define a wire dipole's slope angle guaranteeing equality of the amplitudes of the orthogonal field components, the technique with account of diffraction effects on edges of the finite size screen is developed. It is shown that in defined interval of the observation angles the circularly polarized wave with extremely achievable field amplitude may be formed by a choice of appropriate wire dipole's slope angle and removal from a screen.

articleTitle: Sub-THz all-dielectric metasurface with a single bar per the cell
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The resonance properties of the metasurface were obtained using the pseudo-spectral time domain method. The frequency dependence of transmission and absorption of sub-THz waves passed through metasurface have been measured.

articleTitle: Accurate investigation of coupled plasmonic resonances in a chain of silver nanowires
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: This paper presents investigation of plasmonic properties of coupled metal nanowires arranged to form a finite linear chain. Coupled plasmon resonances of such structures embedded into dielectrics with different dielectric permittivity are studied. The main goals of the paper are to validate true potential of a plasmon nanowire-based structure in sensing applications and to reveal optimized configurations with narrowband plasmonic resonances and enhanced sensitivity.

articleTitle: MAS simulation of plasmonic scatterers
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The Method of Auxiliary Sources (MAS) combined with Model-Based Parameter Estimation (MBPE) technique is applied to numerical simulations of plasmonic nano-structures. The MAS is a numerical technique for the calculation of electromagnetic fields in the frequency domain. The adaptive MBPE algorithm is based on Cauchy's formula and operates in the frequency domain to extrapolate or interpolate from a narrowband set of data to a broadband set of data. The data can be either computed or measured over a specified frequency range. For computed data the sampled values of the function and a few low order derivatives are calculated from a Maxwell solver and are then used to reconstruct the function. The MBPE belongs to the class of auxiliary techniques and can be added to any field solver.

articleTitle: 3D system of randomly detuned ring resonators
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: A homogenization procedure aimed at analyzing a metamaterial designed as a system composed of point magnetic dipoles is presented in this paper. These dipoles represent broad side coupled split ring resonators and/or conducting loops terminated by capacitors. A non-precise fabrication process causes dispersion of the geometrical and material parameters of the resonators, and thus dispersion of their resonance frequencies. The homogenization procedure takes into account random distribution of resonator resonance frequencies with the normal probability distribution. The resonant band of the effective permeability of the metamaterial is significantly widened, the values of both real and imaginary parts of the permeability are reduced. The band of negative permeability real part disappears at high dispersion. The paper also comments on the design of a lens aimed at improving the imaging properties of the MRI system. This lens is composed of cells with cubic symmetry. The proposed homogenization method is verified by measuring the scattering parameters of the metamaterial in a rectangular waveguide, and by proving the isotropic response of the metamaterial of the lens.

articleTitle: Improved method of Optical Coherence Tomography imaging
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) is a modern technique suited for imaging of biological tissue. 2D or 3D imaging via conventional OCT methods requires the use of mechanical scanning that, in turn, represents an important limiting factor for the speed of image acquisition. In this article, the problem of spectral domain OCT using a mathematical approach, which combines Fourier-based analysis and statistical (correlation) analysis is studied and a method for OCT imaging using a planar broadband light beam is proposed. The improved method allows a significant increase of the image acquisition speed compared to the state of the art.

articleTitle: Mathematical model of volume optical interconnection in LiNbO3 crystal
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The mathematical model of volume optical interconnection elements that are formed within the LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> crystal is proposed in the paper. The simulations using this model were conducted. The possibility to reconfigure the structure of optical interconnections was demonstrated.

articleTitle: Configurational resonances in nanocomposite thin films electrodynamics
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The configurational resonances are determined by the values of the polarizabilities of inclusions and morphology of nanocomposite film. Namely, they are determined by the distances between the nanoparticles, concentration, distribution and shape of the nanoparticles. These resonances are evaluated from analysis of the effective susceptibility of the film. A single-oscillator model for the linear response of inclusions material is used. Studying numerically the light absorption of nanocomposite thin film, the conditions of configurational resonances are analyzed to be adjusted independently varying the concentration and shape of the nanoparticles.

articleTitle: Superradiance in Dicke systems: A picture with field correlation functions
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The paper presents mathematical apparatus allowing to calculate the correlation properties of electromagnetic field generated by the Dicke system of two-level emitters. Evolution equations are constructed on the basis of Bogolyubov reduced description method for the system macrostate depicted with energy density of emitters and field amplitudes and binary correlation functions with using ideas of electrodynamics of continuous media. Modern computer calculation tools make it possible to simulate and analyze field states for various space arrangements of emitters; the corresponding mathematical problem is formulated. Glauber correlation functions should be used for diagnosing emission characteristics.

articleTitle: Surface electromagnetic wave in the range of 100–5000 kHz over sea covered by ice (numerical results)
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The article demonstrates that the conditions of LF-MF-HF radio wave propagation over the “ice-sea” structure with highly inductive impedance are more favorable than over the sea without ice because of the appearance of surface electromagnetic waves (SEW). It was determined that the conditions of radio wave propagation over ice paths depend on a frequency, ice thickness and distance from the transmitter within the 100 kHz - 5 MHz range on the paths with ice thickness from 0,6 to 2,7 meters.

articleTitle: Analytic solutions and numerical implementation of the specific electromagnetic wave propagation
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The specific cases of the differential Maxwell equations in the Cartesian coordinate system are considered as the basic mathematical models of electromagnetic wave propagation in the finite spatial and flat guided structures. The general wave equations uniting all scalar components of electromagnetic field vector intensities are got uniformly and are solved irrespectively to the boundary and initial conditions. Several proposed boundary value problems regarding the aforesaid wave PDEs (partial differential equations) simulate mathematically corresponding electrodynamic processes and are solved explicitly in the general manner. The relevant numerical implementation in the framework of the simple discretization procedure is suggested as well.

articleTitle: Calculation of biconical cavity eigenfrequencies by the overlapping domain decomposition method in combination with the collocation method
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: This paper presents a simple technique for the calculation of the eigenfrequencies of biconical cavities using the overlapping domain decomposition method in combination with the collocation method, which converges rapidly with increasing number of collocation point pairs and offers a reasonable computation speed.

articleTitle: Yagi-Uda antennas with impedance wires
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The problem of electromagnetic wave excitation by a vibrators system with variable distributed surface impedance located in free space is solved by the generalized method of induced electromotive forces (EMF). The characteristics of three-element and multi-element Yagi-Uda antennas with variable impedance vibrators are calculated.

articleTitle: EM wave scattering on a set of small particles and creation of materials with desired refraction coefficient and magnetic permeability
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: An overview of authors' results related to EM wave scattering by many small particles, embedded in homogeneous medium, is presented. The particles are the thin (nano) perfectly conducting wires or their properties are described by their boundary impedance. The proposed approach allows one to create the medium with a given refraction coefficient or with a desirable spatially inhomogeneous permeability. The important physical results are explicit analytical formulas for the refraction coefficient n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(x) and magnetic permeability μ(x) of resulting media.

articleTitle: Scattering by an inhomogeneous gyroelectric shell coating a PEC spherical core
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: In this work we investigate the electromagnetic scattering by a perfect electric conductor (PEC) sphere coated by an inhomogeneous gyroelectric spherical shell. We develop a method based on the surface-volume integral equation (SVIE) approach, in conjunction with Dini series expansion (DSE). An orthogonal set of Dini-type spherical vector wave functions (SVWFs) is constructed that directly satisfies the boundary conditions on the conductor's surface, and allows the reduction of the SVIEs to an algebraic form. Validity tests are performed for the developed method and numerical results are given for radar cross section (RCS) computations.

articleTitle: Analysis and improvement of convergence of transverse expansions in excitation problems of irregular impedance waveguides
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Efficiency of cross-section expansions based on the fields of waveguide with ideal walls as basis functions is investigated for impedance waveguides. The criterion of the uniform convergence with respect to the number of expansion terms is obtained. In addition, method of convergence improvement is suggested and illustrated by practical calculations.

Author Keywords: infinite set of linear algebraic equations

articleTitle: Axially-symmetric excitation of the disc-cone by the ring magnetic source
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The rigorous solution of the problem of axially-symmetric TM-wave diffraction by the open end of the bi-cone, which consists of finite and semi-infinite shoulders, is obtained. The structure is irradiated by the ring source of the magnetic current. The mode matching method and regularization technique are applied to obtain the problem solution. The transition from the bi-conical scatterer to the disc-cone is analyzed. The dependences of the far-field pattern from the scatterer parameters are investigated.

articleTitle: Influence of anisotropy on eddy current conductivity measurement
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Analytical expression, describing the complex introduced voltage of attachable eddy current transducer with concentric excitation and measuring coils placed on the surface of non-magnetic conductive plate with uniaxial electrical conductivity anisotropy, is obtained. On the basis of its numerical analysis is show, that the anisotropy causes additional error of electrical conductivity eddy current measurement. The estimation of this error is carry out. It's significantly smaller when amplitude of introduced voltage is used as informative parameter compared to its phase. Error of phase eddy current gauges is essentially independent of generalized testing parameter and is equal 2.4 - 2.5%.

articleTitle: Backscattering of electromagnetic waves by snow particles
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Snow is the most common type of solid precipitation; therefore considerable interest is the development of remote sensing methods for studying the characteristics of snow by solving the inverse problems which based on a detailed study of such precipitation properties. The radar cross sections (RCS) of few snow types in resonant wave band are demonstrated and discussed.

articleTitle: Direct methods of power spectra estimations for radar reflections from rains near ground surface
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The problem of power spectra estimations has been formulated and solved for radar reflections from moderate rains in mm band of electromagnetic waves near ground surface on the base experimental data. The direct classical methods of Bartlett and Welch periodograms have been used to find the main characteristics of the power spectra.

articleTitle: Refraction effects for propagation over terrain
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The physical optics (PO) approximations have been applied for numerical simulations of propagation over uneven terrain. They are compared with results of long term measurements of microwave propagation affected by atmospheric refraction profiles. Moreover, they are used for novel comparison with numerical simulations using parabolic equation method and Fock's spherical surface solution. It is validated that the physical optics could offer trustworthy numerical simulations for diffraction field zone and low altitude propagation for various spatial distributions of the air refraction index.

articleTitle: Modified Theory of Physical Optics and solution for scattering fields from a perfectly conducting parabolic reflector
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The scattering problem from the curvilinear surfaces is introduced by the method of Modified Theory of Physical Optics (MTPO). The method is based on the physical optics (PO) current, on the scaterers' and aperture surfaces. The integral equation is achieved by these currents and the result is found with the stationary phase method and edge-point technique. MTPO can be applied to calculate not only the reflected fields but also to calculate edge diffraction fields of various surfaces. In this paper MTPO method is to be explained in addition to the solution of the scattering (reflection+diffraction) problem on perfectly conducting (PEC) parabolic surface by this method. The comparison with cylindrical surface proves the validity of the solution. Since MTPO is an innovative method, there are so many problems for different geometries which can be solved by this method.

articleTitle: Scattering of electromagnetic waves by inhomogeneous dielectric gratings loaded with conducting strips - matrix formulation of point matching method
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: We have proposed a new method for the scattering of electromagnetic waves by inhomogeneous dielectric gratings loaded with parallel perfectly conducting strips using the combination of improved Fourier series expansion method and point matching method. Numerical results are given for the transmitted scattered characteristics for TE and TM cases.

articleTitle: Wireless body area networks numerical, experimental and approximate characterization
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: For the numerical design of on-body communication components, accurate and reliable models of a communication channel of a wireless body area network (WBAN) are needed. Whereas numerical models (volume-pixel ones, layered ones) can be very detailed, experimental models consist of a single layer of an agar gelatin usually. In the paper, an analytical model based on Norton surface waves is used to describe the surface wave propagating along the interface between the agar phantom and environment. For the frequency band of interest, electrical parameters of the analytical model of the agar phantom are optimized so that the propagation properties of the phantom can agree with properties computed by numerical layered models, volume-pixel models, or experiments.

articleTitle: Plane wave scattering by a double-periodic gyromagnetic layer analyzed by the integral functional method: Full-wave solution
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: We obtained full-wave numerical solution of the problem of the plane wave scattering by a double-periodic gyromagnetic layer with the aid of the method of integral functionals. Using this technique it we found the layer thicknesses corresponding to nearly total transmission in a very wide range of the angles of plane wave incidence.

articleTitle: Interaction of THz radiation with plasmonic grating structures based on graphene
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: We investigated interaction of THz radiation with the graphene-based plasmonic structure which consists of the doped single layer graphene under submicron metallic grating embedded into layered dielectric environment. High-frequency electron transport in graphene was described by the dynamical conductivity dependent on the frequency and wave-vector. The Maxwell equations was solved by the method of the integral equations. We found that spectra of the transmission, reflection and loss coefficients have specific features associated with the plasmon resonances and a singularity of the dynamic conductivity inherent to the Dirac electrons in the graphene. Latter manifest itself as an emergence of the characteristic dips at frequencies ω<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub> = v<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub>q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub>, where v<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</sub> is Fermi velocity of electron gas in graphene and q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub> is the reciprocal grating lattice wave vector. We suggested that observed feature could be used for spectral alignment of optical devices in THz/FIR diapasons.

articleTitle: Wiener-Hopf analysis of the radar cross section of a thin material strip
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The plane wave diffraction by a thin material strip is analyzed using the Wiener-Hopf technique and approximate boundary conditions. An asymptotic solution is obtained under the condition that the strip width is large compared with the wavelength. Applying the saddle point method, the scattered far field is evaluated asymptotically. Numerical results on the radar cross section are presented.

articleTitle: On the Grad method in plasma physics
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: This work is devoted to the investigation of the component distribution functions (CDFs) of a spatially uniform completely ionized plasma in the framework of the Grad problem. The investigation is made on the basis of the Chapman-Enskog method which is generalized with account for relaxation degrees of freedom. It is shown that the widely used results of the 13-moment Grad approximation for the CDFs are the results of the leading order in the small electron-to-ion mass ratio, and corrections to these results of higher orders in the small electron-to-ion mass ratio are obtained.

articleTitle: Microwave circular waveguide with coaxial layer of high lossy liquid
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The electromagnetic wave propagation in a circular metal waveguide with a central cylindrical dielectric rod and coaxial layer of high loss liquid have been studied at the wide frequency range 5-30 GHz with operating HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> waveguide mode. We have obtained phase and attenuation coefficient dependences on frequency and waveguide inner radius. The areas of sharp dependence of the attenuation coefficient at frequency and waveguide inner radius deviation were found. Owing to the high loss liquid the operating frequencies range can be extended from millimeter wavelength range up to centimeter one for the given waveguide structure. The abnormally low attenuation coefficients for waveguide mode HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> in the centimeter wavelength range at certain frequencies and values of thickness of the liquid layer has been found. This waveguide structure can be used for complex permittivity determination of high loss liquids.

articleTitle: Comparison of single station methods for analysis of tweek atmospherics
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Comparative analysis of two different methods for estimation of parameters of the lower ionosphere by tweek - atmospherics was performed. These are so-called the phase and the sonogram methods. The analysis is based on numerical simulations of tweek atmospherics waveforms. The dependency of estimations accuracy of distance to a tweek source and effective ionosphere height were tested against a stochastic noise level. The stochastic error decreases with increasing SNR. The maximum value of a systematic error for SNR - 5 dB is less than 4% for distance determination and it is less than 1% for the height determination.

articleTitle: Determination of hydrometeor parameters using geostationary satellite radio signals
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The opportunity to use the geostationary satellite radio signals at high elevation angles for determining parameters of hydrometeors (rain, snow, hail, clouds) is discussed. The attenuation and scattering of radio waves allow one to determine the average moisture and drop concentration in stratocumulus clouds, the reflection of radio waves from cumulonimbus clouds provides information on the intensity and hazard of cloudbursts etc. The functional diagram of equipment and results of experimental investigations on main forms of low-, middle- and high-level clouds are presented. The method of cloud recognizing using the geostationary satellite radiation, is promising. The equipment is environmentally safe, simple and cheap.

articleTitle: Out-of-band gain characteristics of linear antenna array
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Directional properties of equidistant linear array, consisting of symmetrical half-wave dipole in out-of operating frequency band is discussed. The frequency response of the antenna gain, taking into account the input impedance of the dipoles is calculated.

articleTitle: Accurate analysis of electromagnetic scattering from cylindrical objects located near periodically corrugated surface
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: This paper presents a rigorous spectral-domain formulation of the two-dimensional electromagnetic scattering from a finite array of cylindrical objects located near periodically corrugated surface. The structure under consideration is an imperfectly periodic structure, in which the structural periodicity is locally broken, and the fields generally have continuous spectra in the wavenumber space. The present formulation is a spectral-domain method based on the pseudo-periodic Fourier transform, and combines the coordinate transformation method and the recursive transition-matrix algorithm.

articleTitle: Gyrotropic-nihility state in magnetic superlattices
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Characteristics of the gyrotropic-nihility state are studied in a magnetic superlattice, which is influenced by an external static magnetic field. Investigations are carried out with the assistance of the effective medium theory, according to which the studied structure is approximated as a uniform gyroelectromagnetic medium. The theory of the gyrotropic-nihility state is developed in terms of the eigenwaves propagation in such gyroelectromagnetic medium. It turns out that in the frequency band around the frequency of gyrotropic-nihility state the studied structure appears to be matched to free space with both the refractive index and the wave impedance.

articleTitle: Copula simulation of weather radar inputs
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: This paper presents the copula based simulation of weather radar preprocessed input signals with orthogonal polarizations. The use of copulas allows taking into account their mutual dependence in a straightforward and natural way, because the copula relates exactly to the pure dependence between the marginal distributions.

articleTitle: Real valued TM fields in arbitrary cross section waveguide
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: An arbitrary shape called botanic curve is used for waveguide cross section which is singly connected and has enough smooth form. The boundary value problem is solved with evolutionary equations of electromagnetic theory in time domain. The real valued solutions of fields are subsequently obtained in Hilbert space. The field components depend on transverse coordinates and amplitudes are function of time and axial coordinates. The modal and energetic waves are studied in detail and their dependence on time graphically illustrated for lossy and lossless waveguide.

articleTitle: Fano resonances in dielectric, metallic and metamaterial photonic structures
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: We investigate numerically Fano resonances excited in periodic arrays of dielectric, metallic and left-handed cylinders. Of particular interest are Fano resonances excited in the linear array of cylinders. We analyze spatial distribution and symmetry of electromagnetic field and discuss the relation between observed Fano resonances and frequency spectra of two-dimensional arrays of cylinders.

articleTitle: Nonlocal electrodynamics of helical metals
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: We consider the phenomenon of natural optical activity, and related chiral magnetic effect in helical metals, broadly defined as the ones with spin-momentum locking. To reveal the correspondence between the two phenomena, we compute the optical conductivity of a noncentrosymmetric semimetal to linear order in the wave vector of the light wave, specializing to the low-frequency regime. We show that it is the orbital magnetic moment of quasiparticles that is responsible for the natural optical activity, and thus the chiral magnetic effect. We further extend the treatment to the case of spatially non-uniform systems, and derive the most general microscopic formulae for the gyrotropic tensor that satisfies general Onsager relations.

articleTitle: Effective simulation of a microwave spherical 3-D cavity dielectric resonator using FDTD technique
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: We present FDTD (Finite Difference Time Domain) method use for cavity microwave spherical resonator with some features that allows one to speed up the calculation and use computer memory more effective. Results of such simulation are in good agreement with theoretical prediction for the spherical resonator eigen-frequency spectrum.

articleTitle: Analysis of the E-polarized electromagnetic wave diffraction by an infinite periodical strip grating without one strip
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The E- polarized wave diffraction by an infinite periodic strip grating without single strip is considered. The total field is found as a sum of field of infinite periodical grating and field induced by the removal of a single strip. The problem is reduced to the singular integral equations with additional conditions. The directional patterns and field distribution in the domain above the grating are represented.

articleTitle: Generalized approach to solving the inverse scattering problems on the basis of sampling strategy
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Inverse scattering problems for both perfectly conducting and penetrable obstacles are considered in the paper treating the initial data as a random process that depends on deterministic and random parameters. A general approach is developed to identify boundary of the scatterers based on the far-field pattern. The approach belongs to the set of sampling methods of solving the inverse scattering problem, where indicator functions are established. Numerical simulations confirm that the proposed approach to derive the indicator functions can be successfully applied for the cases of fixed-frequency and multiple-frequency initial data, including back-scattering scenario of measurement.

articleTitle: Influence of moving the primary source field to determine the location of an elongated defect
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: To determine the location of elongated subsurface defects in conductivity materials in the case movement of source primary field on the surface of the object inspection is proposed the method of the correlation processing signals. In base of the method was put the procedure for determining the maximum value square of the correlation coefficient between the theoretically calculated values of the magnetic field of an infinitely long filament with the current (model defect) and measured on the surface of object inspection the values signal from defect. By the numerical experiments are shown efficiency of application of method to processing and analysis of signals of non-destructive eddy current testing.

articleTitle: Boundary integral representation for Beltrami vector fields
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Method of weighted residuals is used for developing of the boundary integral representation for a solenoidal vector field. It is shown that the solenoidal vector in an arbitrary point of domain can be expressed through its values and curls of the different order on the boundary domain. Boundary integral representation for the linear Beltrami vector fields are obtained. The boundary integral equations of the second kind for the solving of the boundary value problems of the second kind are received. It is marked that the given integral equations allow the effective numerical solving. Shown that in the case boundary value problem of the first kind solution can be obtained by quadratures. Showing the relationship between Beltrami vector fields and the solutions of the first boundary value problem for the Helmholtz equation.

articleTitle: Symmetry accounting helps solve the Lasing Eigenvalue Problems for optical microcavities
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The microcavity modes are considered accurately using the linear electromagnetic formalism of the Lasing Eigenvalue Problem (LEP) with exact boundary and radiation conditions. We reduce the original problem to a nonlinear eigenvalue problem for the system of Muller boundary integral equations and build a numerical method accounting symmetry of solutions. Symmetry accounting helps split solutions on classes, which contributes to the stability of calculations and reduces the dimension of the nonlinear spectral algebraic problem.

articleTitle: MBPE for speeding up the computation of plasmonic structurs
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: A Model-Based Parameter Estimation (MBPE) technique is described to accelerate numerical simulations of electromagnetic structures. The adaptive MBPE algorithm is based on Cauchy's formula and operates in the frequency domain to extrapolate or interpolate from a narrowband set of data to a broadband set of data. The data can be either computed or measured over a specified frequency range. For computed data the sampled values of the function and a few low order derivatives are calculated from a Maxwell solver and are then used to reconstruct the function. For measured data, only measured values of the parameter set are used to create broadband information. In this case derivatives are avoided as they are too noisy. Adaptive MBPE belongs to the class of auxiliary techniques and can be added to any field solver. In this paper the technique is combined with two semi-analytic field solvers working in the frequency domain, the Method of Auxiliary Sources (MAS) and the Multiple Multipole Program (MMP). A dielectric waveguide as well as Channel Plasmon-Polariton (CPP) structures are analyzed to demonstrate the efficiency of adaptive MBPE.

articleTitle: Latest advances in computational electromagnetic solvers for highly inhomogeneous anisotropic objects
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Solvers for the electromagnetic scattering (EM) by 3D inhomogeneous anisotropic objects are presented and reviewed in this work. The volume integral equation (VIE) is applied using Galerkin technique in conjuction with Dini series expansion (DSE). However, Galerkin technique leads to the computation of volumetric integrals which is time consuming to evaluate. This method is optimized by applying collocation to the constitutive relation connecting the electric field with the electric displacement. This scheme results in a fast solver which is developed by applying least-squares techniques. This solver is then compared with other available methods that are capable of evaluating the scattering by inhomogeneous anisotropic objects, including the Amsterdam discrete dipole approximation (ADDA), the finite integration technique (FIT), and the finite element method (FEM).

articleTitle: Beam-Propagating Method and Physics behind it - revisited
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: In this paper, in contrary to a common belief that Beam Propagation Method, BPM, is just a mathematical formalism not so much linked to physical phenomena, we intend to show that there is a lot of physical aspects involved. We present several examples that include also the study of radiation field (as extracted from the total beam) propagation along the optical waveguide structures that BPM allows easily to model. This leads to physical explanations of several propagation effects of practical interest.

articleTitle: Scattering of electromagnetic waves by a PEC bar grating with a nonlinear dielectric filling of its slits
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: An analytical algorithm for solution of the diffraction problem on the PEC bars grating with a nonlinear dielectric filling of its slits is constructed. It is based on the solution of the diffraction problem on the PEC bars grating with a piecewise homogeneous linear dielectric filling of its slits.

articleTitle: Effects of prewave zone and electron ‘half-bareness’ in millimeter wavelength transition radiation
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The problem of transition radiation (TR) by ultra-relativistic electron with nonequilibrium electromagnetic field is considered and its spectral-angular characteristics are calculated. The problem of TR registration in the prewave zone is investigated. The expressions for radiation characteristics obtained in this region with the use of detector of arbitrary transversal size are derived.

articleTitle: Ultrathin nonlinear metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: We present a novel class of ultrathin metasurfaces operating in a nonlinear regime, simultaneously providing generation efficiencies that are many orders of magnitude larger than in other nonlinear setups, and, at the same time, capable of controlling the local phase of the nonlinear signal with high precision and subwavelength resolution. The key to achieving such outstanding performance is combining a strong local field enhancement and polarization selectivity of plasmonic nano-antennas with extremely high nonlinearity of multi-quantum well semiconductor stacks. In this work, we discuss the operation principles of such metasurfaces and provide experimental and numerical results. We also show how a savvy application of Lorentz reciprocity principle allows for fast and efficient analysis and modeling of such metasurfaces consisting of thousands of elements.

articleTitle: Numerical modeling the resonance X-band structures with local inhomogeneities inside
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The electrodynamic characteristics of two types of resonators with the local cylindrical inhomogeneities inside are analyzed with the aim to find the conditions of the most effective employment of such resonators as the resonance cells of X-band radio spectrometers. As the results of simulations the optimal geometrical dimensions of the conductive and low loss samples as well as their location in the resonance volume are determined.

articleTitle: 16 - bit data processing system for front-side looking SAR
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: In this paper 16-bit data processing system for the front-side looking synthetic aperture radar is proposed. It is based on the filter having similar principle of construction as a Savitzky-Golay filter. Special properties of matrices used for calculations, allows this system to work in real-time mode. Altera DSP Builder is used for simulation of the system.

articleTitle: Electron wave packet evolution under the influence of random electric field
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: We consider an electron wave packet evolution in the external deterministic electric field with Gaussian white noise addition. An explicit expression was given for the averaged probability flux with Gaussian initial wave function. We show that the noise addition increases wave packet spreading rate, which has a significant influence on flux amplitude and may play both destructive and constructive role. This depends on the form of external deterministic field.

articleTitle: Ray-mode conversion technique applied to thick slit diffraction
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Ray-mode conversion technique has been applied to formulate a plane wave diffraction by a wide and thick slit perforated in a perfectly conducting screen. The internal field inside the thick slit is first formulated by multiply bouncing reflected and diffracted rays, and this ray summation is converted into a summation of parallel plane waveguide modes through the Poisson summation formula. The total field is then expressed as a summation of successive radiation fields excited by the waveguide modes at the aperture edges. The derived results are used to calculate the far fields and compared with the reference solution. Good agreement has been observed to confirm the validity of our formulation.

articleTitle: Predictive map of geoelectric sections of North Eurasia and its application for the radiowaves propagation calculations
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Predictive map of geoelectric sections of the North Eurasia, necessary for calculation of propagation of VLF-MF radio waves, is constructed. Taking into account the layered structure of the underlying medium, this map is capable of increasing the accuracy of electromagnetic field calculations by 1.5-3 times as compared to the Morgan-Maxwell map and ITU-R Recommendation P.832-2. The methodology of the geoelectric mapping is described. The studies of electrical properties of layered media by combined radio and geophysical methods in a variety of natural and geological conditions, and the proposed method of geoelectric mapping have resulted in the construction of a new generation of maps showing the electrical properties of the underlying medium that account for the layered structure of the crust and have no analogues in the world.

articleTitle: Using GNSS signals for measuring the midlatitude atmosphere parameters
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Certain classes of meteorological phenomena and their impact on the GNSS signals propagation were considered. More than 26280 hours of continuous meteorological and navigation observations were processed. The results can be used to create adaptive algorithms of satellite positioning and verification of existing models of the midlatitude atmosphere.

articleTitle: Original Ka-band fractional spiral antennas
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The original fractional $-shape spiral antenna being fed from the Ka-band metal waveguide is proposed. The impedance bandwidth of such an antenna is 6.7GHz. Herewith, the axial ration does not exceed 3dB level within the limits of 34.2 - 37 GHz. The radiation pattern of such an antenna is similar to the monopole antenna with zero-radiation intensity in the antenna axis and with an elevation angle of peak directivity equal to about θ=20°. It is important, that the radiation pattern shape does not undergo any visible deformations through the operational frequency band. The use of near-field technology allows for explaining the basic reasons of the axial ratio changing through the antenna bandwidth. The proposed antenna seems to be very attractive for various practical applications in the millimeter range.

articleTitle: Nonreciprocal combinatorial frequency generation induced by non-Hermitian hyperbolic systems
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The effects of nonreciprocal resonance scattering in the nonlinear loss-compensated semiconductor-dielectric multilayers with hyperbolic dispersion are explored. The three-wave mixing technique is applied to study the nonlinear processes. It is shown that the introduction of gain for dielectric layers can compensate the losses in linear response of the stack and enhance the efficiency of the mixing processes in the stack with passive semiconductor layers with resistive type of nonlinearity. It is shown that weak nonreciprocity of linear response can lead to significant nonreciprocity of nonlinear interaction.

articleTitle: Asymptotic solutions of the second order for LE waves in corrugated rectangular waveguides
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Propagation of LE waves in rectangular waveguides with non-periodical corrugation of the wall are examined. The boundary-value problem is solved by the Krylov-Bogoliubov-Mitropolsky asymptotic method. Mutual conversions of two wave modes propagating in such waveguides are investigated. Coupling coefficients are obtained in analytical form for some particular cases.

articleTitle: Application of the optical theorem to the analysis of lasing thresholds in microlasers with ring-like active regions
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: We study the lasing modes of microlasers with ring-like active regions. We reduce the considered eigenvalue problems to transcendental equations and solve them numerically. The comparison of the spectral characteristics, i.e. the lasing frequencies and the associated values of threshold material gain, of these resonators with previously obtained solutions for fully active resonators has led to the efficient use of the optical theorem.

articleTitle: Benefits of near-field technology in the small-size antenna designing
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: In this paper three different types of small-size antennas are presented with the aim to illustrate the benefits of near-field technology for explaining the features of the antenna performance as well as for designing the antenna with characteristics given in advance. In particular, the axially-symmetrical mono-beam radiation pattern with the radiation maximum in the antenna axis can be realized in the DDA by introducing the additional passive dipoles. At the same time, the use of additional passive phase correctors in the rectangular patch antenna configuration one may change the radiation pattern shape, the elevation angle of peak directivity and antenna bandwidth.

articleTitle: Anomalous dispersion of polaritons in a magnetic-semiconductor superlattice
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Dispersion properties of both bulk and surface polaritons at the interface between vacuum and ferrite-semiconductor superlattice are studied. The superlattice is considered to be influenced by an external static magnetic field in the Voigt geometry. In order to derive tensors of effective relative permeability and effective relative permittivity of the structure under study the homogenization procedure from the effective medium theory is engaged. Peculiarities of polariton dispersion features at a particular extreme gyrotropic-nihility state are revealed and explained.

articleTitle: Analysis of the H-polarized electromagnetic wave diffraction by a semi-infinite periodical strip grating
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The H-polarized wave diffraction problem by the semi-infinite strip grating is considered. The problem is reduced to the singular integral equation with additional conditions. The directional patterns of the field scattered by the end of the grating are represented.

articleTitle: On the Green's functions technique for the numerical solution of inverse boundary problems
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: We consider two types of inverse boundary problems related to the Laplace equation in planar double connected domains. The first one consists in the determining the Cauchy data on an inclusion from given Cauchy data on an accessible exterior boundary. On this accessible part the function (or the normal derivative) is known and, additionally, on a portion of this exterior boundary the normal derivative (or the function) is also given. For this linear inverse problem we propose a direct boundary integral approach in combination with Tikhonov regularization for stable determination of the Cauchy data on the inclusion. To determine these quantities on the inclusion, boundary integral equations are derived using Green's functions. We outline an effective way of discretizing these boundary integral equations based on the Nyström method and trigonomtric approximations. The second set of inverse problems is the reconstruction of the interior curve from the given Cauchy data of a harmonic function on the exterior boundary. With the help of Green's function and potential theory this non-linear boundary problem is reduced to the system of non-linear boundary integral equations. We develop three iterative algorithms for its numerical solution. Full discretization of the linearized systems is realized by a trigonometric quadrature method. Due to the inherited ill-possedness in the obtained system of linear equations we apply the Tikhonov regularization. Numerical results show that the proposed approach gives good accuracy of reconstructions with economical computational cost.

articleTitle: Radioimpedance sounding of gradient semiconducting medium
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Numerical methods and algorithms for solving direct and inverse problems of radioimpedance sounding of gradient semiconducting medium are developed. A program for calculating the surface impedance in view of dependence of conductivity and permittivity of the vertical coordinate is developed. Graphical interpretation method of restoring the structure of gradient semiconducting medium is proposed.

articleTitle: Axially symmetric TM-wave illumination of the sphere-conical resonator
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The axial symmetric TM-wave illumination of the sphere-conical resonator is investigated. The problem is solved rigorously using the analytical regularization technique. Resonator is formed by a perfectly conducting semi-infinite truncated cone with the spherical diaphragm by which one of conical sectors is closed. The electric radial dipole is placed in front of the aperture. The problem is reduced to an infinite system of linear algebraic equations (ISLAE) of the second kind which allows the solution with a given accuracy for any geometrical parameters and frequency. We analyze numerically the sphere-conical resonator excitation. The dependence of the resonance modes radiation through the aperture on the geometrical parameters, as well as the features of the formation of far field patterns are investigated.

articleTitle: Methods of decreasing the lasing thresholds of optical resonators with periodically structured active nano wires
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Periodic wire grating in free space has very high-Q resonances at the frequencies close to the Rayleigh anomalies. We discuss a further enhancement of that effect by sandwiching the grating between two distributed Bragg reflectors (DBRs).

articleTitle: Diffraction of electromagnetic waves by non-uniform metal-dielectric sphere in optical and microwave bands
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: A full wave analytical solution of the problem of EM plane wave diffraction by multilayered metal-dielectric sphere is presented. The proposed solution is based on variable separation method. The high numerical efficiency of the algorithm is achieved due to suggested original recurrence relations for evaluation of the fields within the multilayered sphere. The comparison of the analytical results and results of 3D CAD tool FEKO shows excellent agreement. The extinction cross-sections have been calculated for modern plasmonic materials (TaN, ZrN, HfN, AZO, ITO) in optical band. The proposed solution is used also for analysis of near and far field of antenna systems based on Luneburg lens.

articleTitle: Study of surface plasmon polaritons in heavily-doped GaN structure with surface-relief gratings in terahertz frequency range
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: We present the results of theoretical analysis of recent experimental data on excitations of the surface plasmon polariton in heavily-doped GaN epitaxial layers [1]. Spectra of the reflection coefficient, and their polarization dependencies were investigated in the frequency range of 2-20 THz including the Reststrahlen band of bare GaN. The measured reflectivity spectrum for p-polarized radiation for the sample with the surface-relief grating demonstrate a set of resonances associated with excitations of different surface plasmon polariton modes. The characteristic features of the reflectivity spectrum, namely, frequencies, amplitudes and widths of the resonance dips are well described theoretically based on solution of the Maxwell equations in the frames of the modified technique of rigorous coupled-wave analysis (RCWA). Spectral peculiarities due to the diffraction effect have been also revealed and discussed.

articleTitle: Rigorous RCS analysis of a finite parallel-plate waveguide with material loading
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: A rigorous radar cross section analysis is carried out for a finite parallel-plate waveguide with four-layer material loading using the Wiener-Hopf technique. Exact and approximate solutions of the Wiener-Hopf equations are obtained, and the scattered field is evaluated analytically. Numerical examples on the radar cross section (RCS) are presented for various physical parameters and far-field scattering characteristics of the waveguide are discussed in detail.

articleTitle: BSP step for on-ground targets RCS measuring or calculation
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Currently, an important issue is the evaluation of radar visibility of different complex objects. To achieve this goal it is necessary to receive the BSP for the test object. However, the BSP calculation usually takes most of the time necessary for a comprehensive assessment of radar visibility of the object. In this article we will look at angle step choosing in BSP calculations for objects situated on some underlying surface. For step choosing statistical analysis approach was used.

articleTitle: Accurate circuit models for the analysis of stacked metal gratings
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Stacked periodic planar structures have been a continuous subject of research interest due to their ability to control the polarization, transmission, reflection, and absorption of electromagnetic waves. The scattering of plane waves by one-dimensional (1-D) and two-dimensional (2-D) arrays of metal patches (or apertures) can be accurately modeled using suitable equivalent circuits. The structures obtained by stacking periodic systems of this type can easily be modeled using transmission line sections to account for the dielectric region between the periodic surfaces. However, this task is not straightforward if the separation between the periodically structure surfaces is electrically small. This contribution will describe a methodology to obtain valid and accurate circuit models for tightly spaced periodic arrays of apertures. The proposed theory allows for the modeling of devices that have attracted a lot of attention in recent years, such as the fishnet structures employed to obtain an effective negative index of refraction.

articleTitle: Integral equation method of the expansion type applied to light scattering from nano-metal strips
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: We demonstrate an accurate and powerful numerical solution to the light scattering from a set of nano-strips made of noble metals stacked in parallel. With the aid of the generalized boundary conditions, the problem is formulated into the singular integral equations for unknown electric and magnetic current density on the strip, In the procedure of the moment method, Legendre and Chebyshev polynomials are successively employed as the basis and testing functions. Numerical examples show the the effectiveness of the solution.

articleTitle: Modification of the method of averaged characteristics for multiharmonic problems in high-current electronics devices
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: We carry out the modification of the method of averaged characteristics for solving of multiharmonic problems in high-current electronic devices considering the specific of plural parametric resonances. We demonstrate an application technique of the modified method in terms of a plasma-beam superheterodyne free-electron laser (SFEL) of H-ubitron type with a helical electron beam.

articleTitle: Advanced modal analysis of crossed gratings application to bi-periodic composite materials made of stacks of one dimensional arrays of rods
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: We analyse composite materials made of tilted one dimensional arrays of rods embedded inside a host medium. We use modal methods optimized for rods with rectangular cross sections. We thus obtain an efficient multi purpose code.

articleTitle: Pre-fractal gratings of PEC strips
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: Fundamentals of the electromagnetic theory of pre-fractal strips' gratings (PFSG) are presented. A flat PFSG consists of perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) strips located within a plane according to segments which form a certain stage of a self similar fractal's creation. The problem of wave's scattering by the PFSG is treated in the classically rigorous formulation on the base of the integral equation technique. Considerable attention is focused on the systems analysis of the process of constructing some classes of self-similar fractals with variable Hausdorff dimension. Several mathematical models are used for the process of electromagnetic wave's interaction with the PFSG. Asymptotic models of weakly filled PFSG, which have explicit solutions, are considered in details.

articleTitle: Dynamic resonance in the high-Q and near-monochromatic regime
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: This communication investigates the sensitive behavior of dynamic resonant scattering when an extended system is weakly coupled to a resonator (high-Q) and the source field is nearly monochromatic but of finite energy. We analyze a specific model that incorporates certain universal features of resonance. It is a resonant modification of the Lamb model for the interaction between an oscillator and a continuum. This resonant Lamb model incorporates a two-part scatterer attached to an infinite string with continuous spectrum. The non-resonant part of the scatterer is associated with direct scattering; and the resonant part-an oscillator coupled weakly to the string- is associated with field amplification and delayed scattering. A sharp anomaly in the transmission coefficient occurs when the source frequency is within γ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of the resonant frequency (where γ is the coupling constant and the Q-factor is of order γ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>); this anomaly is mollified as the source spreads spectrally. Resonant amplification occurs when the source frequency is within γ of the resonant frequency. The amount of amplification depends on the relationships between the spectral width γ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of the transmission resonance, the spectral width σ of the source field, and the difference between the source frequency and the resonant frequency.

articleTitle: Examples of analytically regularized scattering problems via Helmholtz decomposition and Galerkin method
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
