abstract: The aim of this paper is the description of a new analytically regularizing procedure, based on Helmholtz decomposition and Galerkin method, successfully employed to analyze the electromagnetic scattering by zero-thickness perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) circular disk and hollow finite-length PEC circular cylinder, even if only the former subject will be presented here for the sake of brevity. After expanding the fields in cylindrical harmonics, the problem is formulated as an electric field integral equation (EFIE) in the vector Hankel transform (VHT) domain. Assuming as unknowns the curl-free and divergence-free contributions of the surface current density, a second-kind Fredholm infinite matrix-operator equation is obtained by means of Galerkin method with suitable expansion basis reconstructing the expected physical behaviour of the surface current density and with closed-form spectral domain counterparts. The coefficients of the scattering matrix are single improper integrals which can be quickly computed by means of an analytical acceleration technique. Comparisons with the literature have been provided in order to show the accuracy and efficiency of the presented technique.

articleTitle: Methods of singular integral and functional equations in dynamic problems of mathematical physics
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: The topic of this presentation concerns the development of rigorous methods of solving some dynamic problems in mathematical physics based on the singular integral and functional equations technique. The material summarizes mainly recent results obtained in the Karpenko Physico-Mechanical Institute in the field of diffraction theory and fracture mechanics. As a result of our researches on inverse scattering will be presented within the corresponding special section, we will not discuss them here and concentrate on the following three topics. Firstly we consider the possible generalization to the two-dimensional case of the singular integral equation method that is well known in the scalar diffraction theory. Direct methods of their numerical solution not requiring analytical inversion of the corresponding singular operators and resulting in finite algebraic systems demonstrate high efficiency particularly for cylindrical structures of arbitrary cross-sectional geometry within a wide frequency range. Basic cubature formula is obtained for applying the mentioned approach to the two-dimensional case. Then some analytical regularization technique for rigorous solution of dual series equations in diffraction theory for conical and wedge-shaped structures is considered. This technique is based on establishing the rule for correct transition to the infinite systems of linear algebraic equations as well as on obtaining the solutions, satisfying all the necessary conditions. These systems are shown to be determined by a pair of operators, which consist of the convolution type operator and the corresponding inverted one. The entries of the inverted operator can be found analytically using the factorization technique. Finally, a new method for solution of the dynamic problems of elasticity theory and fracture mechanics is considered. This approach is based on the application of the modified finite-difference method at time and integral equations for space variables. For zero initial conditions the equations of motion are reduced to homogeneous systems of differential equations for determination of displacements at time nodes. For the two-dimensional dynamic problems of the crack theory the efficient solution of these differential equations is obtained by the boundary integral equation method. The quadrature method is used for numerical solution of the integral equations. A time dependent stress intensity factors are obtained for an elastic plane with rectilinear or curvilinear cracks under action of some impact and impulse tractions.

articleTitle: Low-frequency stable model-order reduction of finite-element models featuring lumped ports
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: A fast frequency sweep method for finite-element models of linear time-invariant structures is presented, which is valid from the static/stationary limit up to the optical range. The key ingredients are a low-frequency stable finite-element formulation and a projection-based method of model-order reduction. The dimension of the reduced model is governed by the complexity of the system dynamics only; it does not depend on the size of the finite-element matrix. A numerical example is presented to demonstrate the efficiency of the suggested approach.

articleTitle: Integral equation analysis of capacitive waveguide circuits
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: This contribution presents a formulation based on the integral equation technique for the analysis of waveguide circuits containing capacitive obstacles, and including material bodies, such as dielectric or magnetic posts. The formulation is very efficient, since it reduces the 3D structure to a 2D problem by using a mixed spatial and spectral formulation. Results show high accuracy and efficiency in the analysis of lowpass filters in waveguide technology. Using the software tool, several new applications in the area of waveguide lowpass filters are introduced. This includes the use of magnetic materials to implement resonant irises, and the use of dielectric materials to reduce multipactor risk in high power applications.

articleTitle: Green's functions for 2D periodic structures and applications to the analysis of waveguide components
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE International Conference on Mathematical Methods in Electromagnetic Theory (MMET)
abstract: In this paper different and efficient acceleration techniques for the evaluation of two-dimensional Green's functions with 1D and 2D periodicities are discussed. The proposed summation numerical methods are based on the appropiate extraction of different asymptotic terms in the spectral domain representation of the corresponding Green's functions. The paper provides insight into the different formulation choices, including numerical results that illustrate the advantages and drawbacks when the techniques are applied to a particular problem. This acceleration techniques allows the implementation of efficient integral equation techniques for the analysis of a wide variety of H-plane microwave passive components composed of conducting and dielectric posts and discontinuities.
